title: Advanced Retrieval Optimization
description: Implement query expansion, query rewriting, multi-query retrieval, and reciprocal rank fusion to maximize RAG retrieval quality.

data.text: Beyond Simple Query to Embedding to Search

Basic RAG retrieves documents using a single embedding query against a vector store. But user queries are often short, ambiguous, or lack the specific terms used in the documents. Advanced retrieval techniques preprocess the query into multiple, richer representations that dramatically improve recall before the LLM even sees the results.

data.text: Query expansion generates multiple search queries from a single user input. The LLM can decompose complex questions into sub-questions (e.g., 'What are the security implications of RAG and how to mitigate them?' becomes two queries: 'RAG security risks' and 'RAG security mitigation'). This increases the chance of retrieving relevant documents that don't match the exact original query phrasing.

data.text: Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines results from multiple retrieval methods (vector search, keyword search, cross-encoder) without needing score normalization. Each result's rank in each method contributes a score of 1/(k + rank), where k is a constant (typically 60). Results appearing in multiple methods get higher fused scores.

data.content: Implementing RRF to combine multiple retrieval backends:

data.text: Hybrid Search: BM25 Plus Vector Search Fusion

Hybrid search combines keyword (BM25) and vector (semantic) search. BM25 excels at exact term matching (e.g., 'CVE-2024-1234'), while vector search captures semantic meaning ('security vulnerability'). RRF or weighted score fusion combines both signals. Azure AI Search, Qdrant, and Weaviate all support hybrid search natively.

For RAG, use query expansion plus multi-query retrieval BEFORE combining with RRF. Do not fuse raw single-query results — decompose first, retrieve, then fuse. This typically improves recall by 20-40% compared to a single vector search.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Query decomposition breaks complex questions into parallelizable sub-queries
Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines multiple ranked lists without score normalization
Hybrid BM25 plus vector search captures both exact terms and semantic meaning
Always decompose before fusing — not after
Cross-encoder reranking is the final precision boost after fusion
data.takeaway: Advanced retrieval is a pipeline: decompose, then retrieve with multiple methods, fuse with RRF, then rerank with cross-encoder. Each stage adds 5-15% RAG accuracy.
